correctness.rationale: All quantifiers and normalization match a simple STS with one approval vote per block. Newton interpolation proves the PAV formula; point/pair incidence and block-union double counts prove each small-seat spectrum, including v=7,9. Universal assertions are not extrapolated from computation.

originality.rationale: Janeczko and Faliszewski 2023 supply Thiele/PAV definitions and general intractability, without these special ballot distributions; Heinlein and Östergård 2022 provide classical configuration techniques but not the voting-winner classification. Actual published research index searches on the exact ballot, score, Pasch and six-seat aliases yielded no covering result. The new mathematical claim is the combined election spectrum and its sharp seat-count non-universality, not classical Steiner counts in isolation.
residual_risks: A prior source could already state the same PAV/Steiner-design translation under different terminology; semantic search failure does not prove uniqueness.

Known design enumeration results strongly imply some of the low-seat combinatorial counts, so the priority claim is confined to the exact election-score/winner spectrum and boundary, not to Steiner block counting itself.

value.rationale: An exact closed-form winner/tie census across every isomorphism class of a natural regular voter design and three to five seats, plus a substantive sharp seat-size threshold where design-independence fails at six seats (same 15 candidates, 420 versus 105 tied PAV optima). This describes what balanced low-order voter statistics can and cannot predict for proportional representation, rather than an arbitrary numeric invariant.
